mission_03: Congratulations on implementing CTC loss and decoding! You now understand the elegant solution that enables end-to-end speech recognition without frame-level alignment. The CTC forward algorithm efficiently sums over all possible alignments between input and output sequences using dynamic programming, and working in log space with np.logaddexp ensures numerical stability even for long sequences. The blank token and repeat rule together allow the model to produce variable-length outputs from fixed-length inputs, handling the fundamental timing mismatch between audio frames and text characters. Greedy decoding provides a fast baseline by collapsing the most likely path, while beam search explores multiple hypotheses to find higher-probability alignments. CTC has been foundational to modern speech recognition, used in DeepSpeech, wav2vec 2.0 fine-tuning, and many other systems. Understanding CTC gives you insight into how sequence-to-sequence models handle the alignment problem without explicit supervision.
